webPolicy.summary: Yes opens a Radio-owned Save dialog only for the question's generation and memory data; otherwise Record off with refresh, nothing erased (record-superseded). No I/O or picker. Disabled with a reason without browser support.
R-RX14 canonical preview and R-RX15 warnings; Choose is its own click, synchronous up to showSaveFilePicker; detail > 1 ignored.
Only recordPulsarWrittenCopy (unchanged R-RX15 proof: owned claim, write, close, bounded fresh exact read-back, current claim, name rule) creates the receipt.

Only a verified receipt continues to the erase question (with a verified note); every other outcome stays in the dialog as an alert; Back (Escape) returns to the unsaved question; nothing erases or arms automatically. Note gate (radioRecordEraseNote): the note is shown only while the current receipt (pulsarWrittenCopy) is for the question's generation with the noted file name and byte count; after a dataset change the plain erase text is shown, Cancel stays the default (the question's origin) and OK is refused record-superseded. Browser continuation is web policy, not the native normal return.

One shared output claim {owner, token} on the current dataset document, taken before the picker and released by the exact owner and token after cleanup; kept across dataset changes; Analysis Save, Analysis raw Download and Radio Choose refuse while it is held.
Radio Save readiness: no lease, no pending analysis read, no output claim; analysis.modal is not a condition (no deadlock). Erase OK still refuses analysis-busy with the receipt kept.
E4 and E9 Yes stay disabled with their reasons.

Attempt tokens and liveness (mounted, route shown, no project operation; a foreign modal does not stop it); abandoned attempts abort open streams and keep the claim until settled; focus: Back on entry, Cancel in the unsaved question, Cancel on the erase question after an async verified Save; wrapping layout at 1440/375/320.

limits: Static disassembly is not CLEA execution, a native exception oracle, x87/GDI/code-page/OS equivalence or physical write durability.
The original Save wrapper's dialog cancellation may return normally; the browser refusal/I-O continuation is explicit web policy.
No hidden or inactive Pulsar Analysis Save is invoked; Radio owns its dialog and attempt.
E4 and E9 stay gated; original VCL effects are not ported.

A browser stage that never settles (most plainly a picker promise) keeps the shared output claim held until that provider promise settles, which blocks both owners across routes: a hung Radio attempt keeps its dialog (Choose, Back, Escape inert) and refuses Analysis Save and raw Download (not-ready); a hung Analysis attempt refuses Radio Choose (not-ready). A route hide or a project operation marks the attempt abandoned (logically dead) but does not release the claim. The application forces no timeout or claim release while the promise is unsettled; a chooser Cancel that rejects the promise (AbortError) settles the attempt normally.

The Radio read-back bound is PULSAR_SAVE_READBACK_MAX_BYTES of the shared Save core (src/core/pulsarSavedCopy.ts), which is the strict PLR reader's PLR_MAX_BYTES itself; the Radio UI does not import the PLR reader.
No original binary bytes or research dumps are copied into the product.
